transcript.heading: News Report One (American Male)
paras: A major retail company announced yesterday that it will be raising the minimum wage for all its employees to 17 dollars per hour starting next month. The decision affects over 300,000 workers across more than 2,000 stores nationwide. Company officials stated that the wage increase is a response to growing concerns about income inequality and the rising cost of living in many cities. The move makes the company one of the highest-paying retail employers in the country. In addition to higher pay, the company will also be expanding its employee benefits package, including increased paid time off and improved health insurance coverage. Industry analysts predict that this decision may put pressure on other large retailers to follow suit, as competition for qualified workers remains intense in the current job market. The company's CEO stated that investing in employees is essential for long-term business success and customer satisfaction.

paras: A powerful earthquake struck a remote mountainous region in Central Asia early this morning, causing significant damage to buildings and infrastructure. The United States Geological Survey reported that the quake had a magnitude of 6.8 and was centered at a depth of approximately 20 kilometers. Local authorities say that at least 45 people have been confirmed dead so far, with more than 200 injured, and rescue teams are still searching for survivors trapped under collapsed buildings. Many villages in the affected area remain cut off due to landslides that have blocked major roads and damaged bridges. The national government has declared a state of emergency and has requested international assistance to support the rescue and relief efforts. Military helicopters have been deployed to deliver food, water, and medical supplies to isolated communities, while temporary shelters are being set up for residents who have lost their homes.

transcript.heading: News Report Three (American Female)
paras: A new study conducted by researchers at Stanford University suggests that walking for just 30 minutes a day can significantly reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke in older adults. The research followed over 13,000 participants aged 60 and above for a period of eight years. The findings indicate that those who engaged in regular moderate walking had a 35 percent lower risk of developing cardiovascular disease compared to those who were mostly sedentary. Interestingly, the study also found that walking at a brisk pace provided additional benefits beyond what was observed with casual strolling. Lead researcher Dr. Patricia Morrison emphasized that exercise doesn't have to be intense to be beneficial—consistent moderate activity can make a substantial difference to long-term health outcomes. The researchers recommend that healthcare providers should prescribe walking programs for older patients as a simple and cost-effective way to improve cardiovascular health.

transcript.heading: Conversation One (British Male + British Female)
paras: Man (Robert): Good morning, Lisa. I was hoping I could talk to you about the Johnson project. We're running into some issues with the timeline.
Woman (Lisa): Oh, hi Robert. Please have a seat. What seems to be the problem? I thought everything was going smoothly last week.
Man: That's what I thought too, but yesterday the client called and asked if we could move the deadline up by two weeks. They want the presentation ready by the 15th instead of the end of the month.
Woman: That's quite a significant change. Did they give a reason for wanting it so much earlier?
Man: Something about their board meeting being rescheduled. They want to present our proposal to the board on the 18th, so they need everything finalized three days before that.

Woman: I see. That puts us in a tight spot. The design team is already working at full capacity on other projects, and the data analysis isn't complete yet. Do we have any flexibility with the client?

Man: I asked if we could at least have until the 20th, but they were quite firm. The 15th is non-negotiable from their perspective. They did mention, however, that they would be willing to pay a rush fee if that helps.

Woman: Hmm, a rush fee certainly helps with overtime costs, but we also need to make sure we don't sacrifice quality. Let me think—if we shift two people from the Thompson account temporarily and bring in the freelance designer we worked with last month, we might be able to pull it off.
Man: I was thinking the same thing about the freelancer. David did excellent work on the Wilson campaign, and he mentioned he had some availability this month.

Woman: Alright, let's do this. You get in touch with David right away and see if he can start Monday. I'll speak with the head of design about reallocating staff. Also, let's schedule a team meeting for this afternoon to go over the revised timeline and make sure everyone understands their priorities.
Man: That sounds like a plan. Should I draft an email to the client confirming we can meet the new deadline?
Woman: Yes, but hold off on sending it until after we've confirmed David is available and the design team can adjust their schedules. I don't want to promise something we can't deliver.

Man: That's actually not too bad compared to some of the other places we've looked at. What about the location? How far is it from campus?

Woman: That's one of the best parts—it's only a 15-minute walk to the main quad, or 5 minutes by bike. There's also a bus stop right outside the building that goes directly to the student union every 10 minutes.

Also, the lease starts August 1st, which means we'd have to sign by next week and pay a security deposit equal to one month's rent.

transcript.heading: Passage One (British Male)
paras: The concept of a four-day work week has gained significant attention in recent years as companies and employees look for ways to improve work-life balance without sacrificing productivity. The idea is simple: instead of the traditional five 8-hour days totaling 40 hours per week, employees work four days for a total of 32 hours while receiving the same pay and benefits. Several large-scale trials conducted in countries around the world have yielded surprisingly positive results. In one major study involving over 60 companies and 2,500 workers in the United Kingdom, revenue increased by an average of 1.4 percent compared to the same period the previous year, while staff turnover dropped by an impressive 57 percent. Employees reported lower levels of stress and burnout, improved sleep quality, and more time to spend with family, exercise, and pursue personal interests. Many companies also noted that meetings became more efficient and that workers were better able to focus on important tasks without the usual Friday fatigue. Critics, however, argue that a four-day week may not be suitable for all industries. Retail, healthcare, and customer service roles often require coverage five or more days per week, making it difficult to implement such a schedule without hiring additional staff, which could offset cost savings. Additionally, some managers worry that maintaining team communication and collaboration could become more challenging when people have different days off. Despite these concerns, the success of early trials suggests that flexible working arrangements will likely become an increasingly common feature of the modern workplace.

transcript.heading: Passage Two (American Female)
paras: Public libraries have transformed dramatically over the past two decades, evolving from quiet buildings filled primarily with books into dynamic community centers that offer a wide range of services and resources. While books remain an essential part of what libraries offer, today's patrons can access far more than just printed materials. Most modern public libraries provide free high-speed internet access and computer workstations, which is particularly valuable for people who don't have internet at home or need a place to work remotely. Many libraries also lend out a surprising variety of items beyond books, including musical instruments, board games, cooking equipment, camping gear, and even tools. Another significant development is the range of programs and events libraries now host. These include not only traditional story hours for children but also job search workshops, language classes, coding clubs for teenagers, tax preparation assistance for seniors, and community meetings on local issues. Libraries have also become important resources for people experiencing homelessness, offering a safe, climate-controlled space where individuals can rest, use the bathroom, and access information about social services. During the COVID-19 pandemic, many libraries demonstrated their flexibility and value by offering curbside pickup of books, providing free Wi-Fi in parking lots, and hosting virtual events. The role of librarians has expanded as well—they now serve as informal tech support, research assistants, career counselors, and community connectors. Despite predictions that the internet would make libraries obsolete, usage has actually increased in many communities, proving that these institutions remain vital and adaptable public resources.

transcript.heading: Passage Three (British Female)
paras: Body language, the non-verbal signals we send through posture, gestures, facial expressions, and eye contact, plays a crucial role in how we communicate with others, often conveying more meaning than the words we speak. Research suggests that between 60 and 70 percent of human communication is non-verbal, making it essential to understand if we want to interact effectively with people from different backgrounds. One important aspect of body language is personal space—the physical distance people maintain between themselves and others during conversation. This distance varies significantly across cultures: people from North America and Northern Europe typically prefer a larger personal space bubble of about an arm's length, while those from Southern Europe, Latin America, and the Middle East often feel comfortable standing much closer together. Eye contact is another area where cultural differences can lead to misunderstandings. In Western cultures, maintaining steady eye contact during conversation is generally seen as a sign of honesty, confidence, and engagement. However, in many East Asian and African cultures, prolonged direct eye contact, particularly with someone in a position of authority, can be viewed as disrespectful or confrontational. Gestures also have different meanings across cultures. The "thumbs up" sign, for example, is considered a positive gesture in the United States and much of Europe, but it is highly offensive in countries such as Iran and Afghanistan. Similarly, nodding the head up and down means "yes" in most cultures, but in parts of Greece and Bulgaria, this gesture can actually mean "no." These differences highlight why it's important to educate ourselves about cultural norms before traveling or working with people from other countries. Being aware of non-verbal communication differences can prevent misunderstandings and help build stronger, more respectful relationships across cultural boundaries.
